speakers.name: Crystal Ivanko (labelled Speaker 9; on for John Ivankoe)
Zach Ogden (introduced as Zach Fadem; on for Andrew Charles)

exchanges.question: Do repeat 'pantry' LTOs like Chicken al Pastor still deliver equal or better lift each time they return; and is value perception improving to reflect generous portions and long-standing underpricing versus the industry?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle Honey Chicken performed better the second time, as many LTOs do, though there is likely a point of diminishing returns around the fifth or sixth time; menu innovation has ramped to 4x what it was a couple of years ago with new items coming in the months ahead. The brand tracker showed solid value-perception progress across all income groups and age cohorts, and Q2 affordability scores were the best in probably the past couple of years; value also includes convenience, execution, innovation and the high-protein menu.

exchanges.question: Investors push back that Chipotle is spending a lot to get only 1%-2% same-store sales growth; what gives confidence that momentum builds into 2027 despite tough comparisons and recent slowdown?
exchanges.answer: Q2 transaction growth reflected early Recipe for Growth results, especially menu innovation, while HEAP, throughput and hospitality investments show proof points in guest satisfaction, food quality and consistency. Additional drivers — menu innovation, deeper rewards engagement, stronger brand communication and group occasions — are showing green shoots and will build through H2 2026 into 2027; he cited unshared digital ideas from Arlie Sisson and creative ambition from Fernando Machado.

exchanges.question: What underlies the full-year low-single-digit comp guide, including Q3 to date, the recent softening and expected cadence?
exchanges.answer: Traffic improved through Q2 and into the first half of July; in the second half of July comps softened about 200 basis points amid the industry Cyclospora issue. Q3, the toughest lap of the year, is expected at around plus 1%, assuming that roughly 200 basis point impact continues; year-to-date performance and Q3/Q4 plans supported raising the full-year guide to low single digits. Boatwright: Chipotle is impacted on sales but not involved in the Cyclospora issue; implicated products are not on its menu and its lettuces are sourced in California.

exchanges.question: What is the incremental capex, expected sales uplift and timeline of refreshing 1,000-1,500 North American stores; and would Chipotle use partners in other international markets instead of owning stores?
exchanges.answer: Chipotle has never done an aesthetic remodel; it is stage-gating a remodel/refresh program this year across several locations and geographies at $100,000-$300,000 per restaurant to test returns, with nothing to report yet. Internationally it will own and operate Western Europe and grow from that base, with the rest of the world partner-operated via partners such as Alshaya (Middle East), Alsea (Latin America) and SPC (Southeast Asia), through partner-operated or JV structures.

exchanges.question: Digital sales grew about 18% year over year after accelerating four quarters ago; was there a big catalyst, and is it linked to changes at the register around loyalty and payment?
exchanges.answer: It is all linked: last year's Summer of Extras taught what works in digital, informing the rewards relaunch that removed app friction and added flexibility to earn and redeem, and this year's Summer of Extras accelerated digital revenue. Chipotle also benefited from an emerging trend, and Arlie Sisson's holistic approach should bring 'game changing' digital commerce innovation over the coming weeks and months.

exchanges.question: Will HEAP labor savings all be reinvested into the production line, and could that drive traffic and customer satisfaction?
exchanges.answer: Yes; HEAP yields about two to four hours of efficiency depending on volume, which is kept in-restaurant for morning prep and peak line deployment, lifting Max 15 throughput, total sales and taste-of-food scores. HEAP will be in 2,000 restaurants by year-end, with the entire portfolio hoped to be complete sometime in 2027; all new restaurants come standard with HEAP.

exchanges.question: Why is 350 company-operated openings per year the right level versus the prior ceiling of 400, and what is the gating factor to accelerating above 350?
exchanges.answer: Given U.S. white space and the ability to develop ready-now leaders, one restaurant per day is meaningful growth the organization can support; going beyond 350 risks diminishing returns in openings or fracturing the base. Incremental growth will come from company-owned Western Europe and partner-operated markets, which will ramp quickly — Alshaya already has 15 restaurants across three or four countries after a couple of years, with meaningful acceleration for 2027 — so Chipotle can still target its historical growth number.

exchanges.question: With a new brand chief, where will positioning go given the For Real campaign may have gone stale, and will value and ingredient quality be highlighted more prominently versus limited-service competitors?
exchanges.answer: For Real was extraordinary and served the brand for many years; Fernando Machado's work is the next evolution, not a 180 pivot. Expect more on fresh in-restaurant prep, ingredient usage and cultivating a better world, with stretched creative ambition; value will be highlighted not via price points or discounts but as the best ingredients prepared fresh daily, with abundance and speed at an approachable price point.

exchanges.question: Does the roughly 1% Q3 comp guide imply about 3% underlying trend with a 2% Cyclospora headwind assumed for the rest of the quarter; and where is system Max 15 throughput for non-HEAP stores?
exchanges.answer: Yes, that is correct; expense guidance is based on the 1% comp guide assuming the impact continues through the quarter, which is very difficult to predict. HEAP restaurants do about two or three more entrees in Max 15; overall in-store is in the low 20s, digital (almost 40% of sales) in the mid-teens, and combined low to mid-30s per restaurant per day.

exchanges.question: What is working in promoting loyalty in-restaurant and what can improve; and do the roughly 80% of in-store transactions without loyalty over-index to lower-income guests?
exchanges.answer: No, non-loyalty in-store transactions are broad-based rather than lower-income. The current experience of fumbling with the app and a card is 'clunky'; in August Curt's team will introduce one-stop pay that earns points on payment and allows enrollment, running behind the scenes without burdening crews or throughput. More consumer education on loyalty in-restaurant is needed.

exchanges.question: Are the new menu items coming in the months ahead center-of-the-plate items or sides, and what detail can be provided?
exchanges.answer: The culinary team has been expanded to drive new news, not just pantry items; work is focused on center-of-the-plate items, with teams also on beverages, sides and desserts. Some big ideas have been pushed through the stage-gate process and could appear on the calendar maybe in the back half of 2026, but certainly in 2027.

exchanges.question: How did Q2 and Q3-to-date trends look by age and income, and are pressured younger and lower-to-middle income cohorts improving relative to higher income, including frequency differences?
exchanges.answer: The younger and lower-income cohorts improved the most; Q1 into Q2 results were broad-based but with outsized impact in those groups, driven by Chipotle Honey Chicken, Cilantro Lime Sauce, promotions like the Matchday BOGO and rewards. Boatwright: Q2 saw the highest year-over-year wallet share gains since 2024, and Chipotle has taken share in each month of 2026 across all income and age cohorts.

exchanges.question: What is the margin outlook beyond Q3, including the gap between pricing and inflation narrowing near year-end?
exchanges.answer: The price-inflation gap was widest in the first half, with pricing in the 1% range versus inflation in the low to mid 3%. In Q3 inflation is expected closer to about 3% with pricing in the mid 2% range, and from Q4 forward the two are expected to match, eliminating the dislocation.

exchanges.question: Did the World Cup create regional divergences that benefited Chipotle; and what has the methodical pricing rollout taught, giving comfort to trend toward the high end of the 1%-2% guide?
exchanges.answer: About 300 restaurants within roughly 10 miles of World Cup stadiums saw a 50 to 100 basis point comp benefit during the tournament, but the overall quarter impact was less than five basis points. The rolling market-by-market pricing approach is working, allowing precise measurement of resistance and adjustment to inflation; Chipotle will continue the strategy, and the dislocation was just a timing impact.

exchanges.question: How much do LTOs contribute to frequency and traffic given the stepped-up cadence; and do high-protein offerings attract existing guests or a new cohort?
exchanges.answer: No specific LTO lifts are disclosed, but Chipotle Honey Chicken and Chicken al Pastor raised transactions from frequent guests and new guests, typically hundreds of basis points of transaction lift mostly sustained through the promotion, with stickiness after; seen as a multi-year AUV lever. Boatwright: protein LTOs bring in new customers, and trying an LTO materially raises lifetime value; expect a couple more center-of-the-plate items in H2 plus sides and a more meaningful push into beverage.
